top_comments.text: My mom and brother can go somewhere once and never get lost. As mom gets older, she is losing some of that ability. My dad and I take after his dad…zero sense of direction. I turned the map when I turned a corner so I could figure out if I had to go left or right at the next turn. This was in like 1995 when my attention span was still normal. When GPS came out, I was so happy because finally FINALLY I could navigate without too many tears. The thing is, I had almost perfect recall at that time. I could tell you what I ate for breakfast a week ago, which outfit I had on, and I was a straight A student who never forgot ANYTHING! But I could go somewhere 100 times and still make wrong turns and need a GPS. I can know exactly where I’m at in a town I’ve lived in for 15 years but have no clue how to get to where I’m going. I lived in Michigan by the west coast and I would drive towards the setting sun until I hit Lake Michigan, then figure out which town I was in to decide if I had to go north or south on 31 to get home. Often I was an hour or two out of my way, but at least I got home. It was frustrating and scary all at the same time. If I don’t have GPS, I don’t want to go more than a few miles from home and only on a familiar road!
